audience: An operator studying how deterministic workflow graphs and coding agents should divide software-engineering work.
problem: A strong coding model is often asked to spend inference on setup, routing, retries, and validation that ordinary software can perform more reliably, while design-oriented app builders can be fast at scaffolding but weak at hard debugging.
solution: A study lab that pins existing OSS and project references, reuses a mature frontend substrate, makes deterministic graph edges explicit, and invokes a coding worker only on unresolved semantic failures.
boundaries: GitHub repository setup is not proof that local Docker, Node, browser, or coding-agent runs succeed.
No paid model is required on the baseline path.
Downloaded source checkouts remain local under .sources and are not vendored into git.
